assumptions: source assumption: carrying capacity K is the maximum population size the environment can support over the modeled interval (source definition).

source assumption: the logistic framing in which this fraction moderates growth; at N far below K the fraction is near 1 (exponential-like growth) and near K it approaches 0 (growth 'slowed greatly or even stopped').

gaps: Quantity meanings carrying_capacity, standing_population and available_fraction are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot; runtime projection omitted.

models.inverse_notes: Standing population is recoverable as N = K*(1 - F). Substitution check: F = 0.8 with K = 1000 gives N = 200, consistent with the ordinary reference. F = 0 gives N = K (population at capacity); negative F (N above K) predicts decline rather than growth, which the page explicitly allows. K = 0 is excluded (capacity must be positive for the fraction to exist).
limitations: A bookkeeping fraction of the logistic model, not a growth prediction by itself; realized dynamics need the full logistic product, which is out of scalar profile.
Assumes a fixed K over the interval; the source notes real carrying capacities shift with conditions.

references.method: Constructed check at round numbers: (1000 - 200)/1000 = 0.8, i.e. 80 percent of capacity still available; verifies encoding, no field value claimed.
references.provenance: Independently constructed arithmetic check; not a published field value.

references.method: Boundary with source meaning: at N = K the fraction is 0, the page's 'growth will be slowed greatly or even stopped' condition.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check tied to the source's at-capacity statement.

rejection_cases.reason: Available fraction of a zero carrying capacity is undefined; K must be positive.
Standing population N is required; capacity alone does not determine the available fraction.

relationship.locator: Section 45.3 'Carrying Capacity and the Logistic Model': ''K - N' ... 'K - N' divided by 'K' is the fraction of the carrying capacity available for further growth.'
relationship.original_equation: (K - N) / K = fraction of the carrying capacity available for further growth
relationship.translation_notes: Source sentence formalized directly; K (carrying capacity) preserved, N (population size) mapped from the page's N, F introduced for the fraction. Dimensional check: (count minus count) over count gives a dimensionless fraction, possibly negative when N exceeds K.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: K is the maximum population size the environment can support; (K - N)/K is the fraction of carrying capacity available for further growth; near 1 when N is small, near 0 when N is large, negative when N exceeds K (decline).

assumptions: source assumption: per-capita birth rate b is uniform over the population and constant over the stated interval, so the total scales linearly with N (source: 'B (birth rate) = bN').
source assumption: B counts births in the same interval over which b is defined; interval bookkeeping must match for b, N and B.

gaps: Quantity meanings per_capita_birth_rate, standing_population and total_births are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot; runtime projection omitted.

models.inverse_notes: Per-capita rate is recoverable as b = B / N for nonzero N. Substitution check: 500 / 1000 = 0.5, consistent with the ordinary reference. N = 0 gives B = 0 (no individuals, no births) and is admissible; recovering b from an empty population is impossible, which is expected. The symmetric death-rate sentence D = dN is intentionally not duplicated: it is the same scaling rule applied to deaths, noted here instead of published as a separate record.
limitations: Interval accounting only; with changing per-capita rates the product must be re-evaluated per sub-interval.
Realized recruitment additionally reflects deaths and migration, which this record excludes by construction.

references.method: Constructed check: per-capita rate 0.5 over 1000 individuals gives 500 births by direct multiplication; verifies encoding, no field value claimed.
references.provenance: Independently constructed arithmetic check; not a published field value.

references.method: Boundary: a zero per-capita birth rate yields zero births regardless of population size.
references.provenance: Definitional boundary check with explicit meaning (no reproduction in the interval).

rejection_cases.reason: Per-capita birth rates cannot be negative.
Population size N is required; a per-capita rate alone does not determine the birth total.

relationship.locator: Section 45.3 'Exponential Growth': 'B (birth rate) = bN (the per capita birth rate 'b' multiplied by the number of individuals 'N')'.
relationship.translation_notes: Source symbols B, b, N preserved exactly. Dimensional check: per-capita rate (1/time) times count gives events per time, i.e. a total rate over the interval. The symmetric D = dN sentence is documented in inverse notes rather than duplicated.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: the birth rate B equals the per-capita birth rate b times the number of individuals N (and symmetrically D = dN); births minus deaths over the interval drive the change in numbers.

assumptions: source assumption: exactly the three genotype classes at a two-allele diploid locus exhaust the census, so their frequencies complete the whole (source: 'these genotypes frequencies will sum to one: p2 + 2pq + q2 = 1').

gaps: Quantity meaning genotype_frequency is not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot; runtime projection omitted.

models.inverse_notes: Any one class frequency is recoverable given the other two (e.g. faa = 1 - fAA - fAa); the record fixes fAA as output only as the serialization choice. Substitution check: 1 - 0.42 - 0.09 = 0.49, consistent with the pea reference. Full fixation of one class (the other two zero) gives 1 and is admissible.
limitations: Two-allele, three-class censuses only; multi-allele systems need the fuller summation (separate three-allele record).
A bookkeeping complement, not an equilibrium prediction; it holds regardless of evolutionary forces.

references.method: Published self-check frequencies: heterozygotes 160/500 = 0.32 and recessives 20/500 = 0.04 leave 1 - 0.32 - 0.04 = 0.64 for dominant homozygotes, matching the keyed 320/500.
references.provenance: Published result (printed class frequencies of the worked self-check) recombined through the summation constraint.

references.method: Figure 19.2 frequencies: Yy .42 and yy .09 leave 1 - 0.42 - 0.09 = 0.49 for YY, matching the printed .49.
references.provenance: Published result (printed class frequencies of the figure) recombined through the summation constraint.

rejection_cases.reason: Class frequencies summing above 1 (0.7 + 0.5 = 1.2) cannot come from one complete census.
Recessive frequency faa is required; one class alone does not determine the complement.

relationship.translation_notes: Summation constraint solved for the homozygous-dominant frequency as the single-output serialization; no separate record is published for the other two solve directions. Dimensional check: pure number minus dimensionless frequencies gives a dimensionless frequency.
